eyebrow: A PRAYER SERIES ON THE THING YOU CAN'T SEEM TO STOP
coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For When You Keep
Doing It Again
coverDek: For the habit you've promised yourself you'd quit a hundred times, the shame that comes after, and the mercy that's still there the morning after — five prayers for breaking free, one honest day at a time.

points.hook: I hate what I keep doing, and I still keep doing it.
paragraphs: There's a strange kind of exhaustion that comes from fighting the same battle over and over — swearing it's the last time, and then finding yourself right back where you started before the week is even over. I'm learning that hating what I do is not the same as being disqualified by it; Paul wrestled with this exact thing and still called himself a work in progress, not a lost cause. Lord, meet me in the gap between who I want to be and who I keep being, and don't let shame talk me out of trying again tomorrow.
points.verseText: For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I.

points.hook: I decree: this stronghold does not get to keep my name.
paragraphs: I decree over my life tonight that whatever has gripped me is not stronger than the One who lives in me — in the name of Jesus, every stronghold built by repetition, secrecy, and shame is pulled down right now! The weapons I'm fighting with are not just willpower and good intentions; they are mighty through God, and mighty is enough. I am not negotiating with this habit anymore — I am declaring war on it, and I already know how this war ends.
points.verseText: For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds.

points.hook: Notice what happens in your chest right before you reach for it again.
paragraphs: Notice the exact moment it happens — the restlessness, the ache, the small voice that says just this once, just to feel normal again. That urge in your body isn't proof you're weak; it's information, a door you can learn to recognize before you walk through it. Before you numb it or chase it, let the Lord meet you in that very tightness and give you a clean heart in the place where the craving lives, not just forgiveness after the fact.
points.verseText: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.

points.hook: Somebody in this church is hiding a relapse they're terrified to say out loud.
paragraphs: Family, somebody in this room went back to the thing they promised everyone they were done with, and right now they are more afraid of being found out than they are hopeful about being free. You were never meant to carry a secret struggle alone and call that faith — Scripture tells us to restore one another gently, to bear what's too heavy to carry solo. If that's you today, let someone in before the silence gets heavier than the sin ever was.
points.verseText: Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness... Bear ye one another's burdens.

points.hook: Child, this morning is not a continuation of last night's failure.
paragraphs: Child, I see every time you've gone back, and I also see every time you've gotten back up, and I want you to know that neither one has changed how I feel about you. My compassions do not run out, and they are not rationed based on how many times you've needed them before — they are new again this morning, made fresh just for you. Stop waiting until you've earned a clean slate to come to Me; I am not waiting for that either.
points.verseText: It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.

cta.closingLine: If even one of these named the fight you're in, you don't have to win it alone — come back tomorrow for the next series.
